title: Clean Architecture in Ruby — Quick Revision

sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: Senior Ruby interviews at product companies often ask about moving beyond Rails conventions to more explicit architectures. Hexagonal architecture in Ruby uses duck-typed interfaces (Ruby Protocols via respond_to?) as ports and plain Ruby objects as adapters, keeping the domain layer free from Rails specifics. The dry-rb ecosystem — dry-validation, dry-types, dry-monads, dry-transaction — provides type safety and explicit error handling in a language that otherwise has neither. DDD in Ruby is less common than in Java but still appears at domain-heavy companies. This page covers the practical trade-offs: Rails' ActiveRecord-as-domain-model is fast to build and hard to test in isolation; hexagonal is slower to build and significantly easier to test at the unit level. The interview answer requires knowing both sides.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: hexagonal-in-ruby, dry-rb, ddd-ruby, scenario-based. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
